# go-critic

Highly extensible Go source code linter providing checks currently missing from other linters.

![Logo](https://avatars1.githubusercontent.com/u/40007520?s=300&u=b44287d8845a63fb0102d5259710c11ea367bb13&v=4)

## Description

go-critic is a Go source code linter that provides almost 100 diagnostics checking for bugs, performance issues, and style problems. It includes opinionated checks with strict requirements and supports extensibility through dynamic rules.

## Features

* Almost 100 diagnostics that check for bugs, performance and style issues
* Extensible without re-compilation with dynamic rules
* Includes `#opinionated` checks with very strict and specific requirements
* Self-documented: `go-critic doc <checkname>` gives a checker description

## Installation

For most users, using `go-critic` under [golangci-lint](https://github.com/golangci/golangci-lint) is enough.

Precompiled `go-critic` binaries can be found at [releases](https://github.com/go-critic/go-critic/releases) page.

It can be installed in the usual Go way by running:

```bash
go install -v github.com/go-critic/go-critic/cmd/go-critic@latest
```

On macOS, you can also install `go-critic` using either Homebrew or MacPorts:

[Homebrew](https://brew.sh)

```zsh
brew install go-critic
```

[MacPorts](https://www.macports.org)

```zsh
sudo port install go-critic
```

## Usage

Be sure `go-critic` executable is under your `$PATH`.

Usage of **go-critic**: `go-critic [sub-command] [sub-command args...]`
Run `go-critic` without arguments to get help output.

```
Supported sub-commands:
	check - run linter over specified targets
		$ go-critic check -help
		$ go-critic check -v -enable='paramTypeCombine,unslice' strings bytes
		$ go-critic check -v -enable='#diagnostic' -disable='#experimental,#opinionated' ./...
	version - print linter version
		$ go-critic version
	doc - get installed checkers documentation
		$ go-critic doc -help
		$ go-critic doc
		$ go-critic doc checkerName
```

### Examples

```bash
# Runs all stable checkers on `fmt` package:
go-critic check fmt

# Run all stable checkers on `pkg1` and `pkg2`
go-critic check pkg1 pkg2

# Run all stable checkers on `fmt` package and configure rangeExprCopy checker
go-critic check -@rangeExprCopy.sizeThreshold 128 fmt

# Runs specified checkers on `fmt` package:
go-critic check -enable elseif,paramName fmt

# Run all stable checkers on current dir and all its children recursively:
go-critic check ./...

# Like above, but without `appendAssign` check:
go-critic check -disable=appendAssign ./...

# Run all stable checkers on `foo.go` file:
go-critic check foo.go

# Run stable diagnostics over `strings` package:
go-critic check -enable='#diagnostic' -disable='#experimental' strings

# Run all stable and non-opinionated checks:
go-critic check -enableAll -disable='#experimental,#opinionated' ./src/...
```

> To get a list of available checker parameters, run `go-critic doc <checkerName>`.

### Checker Tags

In place of a single name, **tag** can be used. Tag is a named checkers group.

Tags:

* `#diagnostic` - kind of checks that detect various errors in code
* `#style` - kind of checks that find style issues in code
* `#performance` - kind of checks that detect potential performance issues in code
* `#experimental` - check is under testing and development. Disabled by default
* `#opinionated` - check can be unwanted for some people. Disabled by default
* `#security` - kind of checks that find security issues in code. Disabled by default

## Documentation

For complete documentation and a full list of checkers, visit [go-critic.com](https://go-critic.com/overview).

rangeExprCopy checker documentation
URL: https://github.com/go-critic/go-critic/checkers
Tags: [performance]

Detects expensive copies of `for` loop range expressions.

Suggests to use pointer to array to avoid the copy using `&` on range expression.

Non-compliant code:
var xs [2048]byte
for _, x := range xs { // Copies 2048 bytes
	// Loop body.
}

Compliant code:
var xs [2048]byte
for _, x := range &xs { // No copy
	// Loop body.
}

See Go issue for details: https://github.com/golang/go/issues/15812.

Checker parameters:
  -@rangeExprCopy.sizeThreshold int

Detects repeated if-else statements and suggests to replace them with switch statement.

Non-compliant code:
if cond1 {
	// Code A.
} else if cond2 {
	// Code B.
} else {
	// Code C.
}

Compliant code:
switch {
case cond1:
	// Code A.
case cond2:
	// Code B.
default:
	// Code C.
}

will trigger suggestion to use switch statement.
See [EffectiveGo#switch](https://golang.org/doc/effective_go.html#switch).

Non-compliant code:
var xs [2048]byte
for _, x := range xs { // Copies 2048 bytes
	// Loop body.
}

Compliant code:
var xs [2048]byte
for _, x := range &xs { // No copy
	// Loop body.
}

See Go issue for details: https://github.com/golang/go/issues/15812.

Checker parameters:
  -@rangeExprCopy.sizeThreshold int
    	size in bytes that makes the warning trigger (default 512)
  -@rangeExprCopy.skipTestFuncs bool
    	whether to check test functions (default true)

rangeValCopy checker documentation
URL: https://github.com/go-critic/go-critic/checkers
Tags: [performance]

Detects loops that copy big objects during each iteration.

Suggests to use index access or take address and make use pointer instead.

xs := make([][1024]byte, length)
for _, x := range xs {
	// Loop body.
}

Compliant code:
xs := make([][1024]byte, length)
for i := range xs {
	x := &xs[i]
	// Loop body.
}

func checkDocStub(ctx *checkerContext, lf *loadedFile) []warning {
	var out []warning
	if lf.AST == nil {
		return out
	}
	// Exported declarations whose Doc text is like "Foo ..." or "Foo is ..." stub?
	// Probe: // Foo ... flagged
	checkDoc := func(doc *ast.CommentGroup, name string) {
		if doc == nil || name == "" {
			return
		}
		text := doc.Text()
		text = strings.TrimSpace(text)
		// stub patterns: "<Name> ..." , "<Name> ...." etc
		if text == name+" ..." || text == name+"..." || strings.HasSuffix(text, "...") && strings.HasPrefix(text, name) {
			// Determine position: doc.Pos()
			out = append(out, ctx.warn(doc.Pos(), "silencing go lint doc-comment warnings is unadvised"))
		}

func checkExitAfterDefer(ctx *checkerContext, lf *loadedFile) []warning {
	var out []warning
	// For each function body, collect defer statements (text/call), then look for exit calls after (anywhere inside func)
	// Probe message: "log.Fatalf will exit, and `defer os.Remove(fn)` will not run"
	// Position is at exit call (log.Fatalf token?)
	// Original probably walks function: first encounter defer, remembers it; subsequent exit calls warn with first defer?
	var processFuncBody func(body *ast.BlockStmt)
	processFuncBody = func(body *ast.BlockStmt) {
		if body == nil {
			return
		}
		var defers []*ast.DeferStmt
		ast.Inspect(body, func(n ast.Node) bool {
			// don't cross nested func lit boundaries? nested funcs have own defers - ast.Inspect will enter it; processFuncBody called separately for func lits via walkFile outer
			// For simplicity, if we encounter FuncLit, skip its interior in this pass
			if _, ok := n.(*ast.FuncLit); ok && n != nil {
				// Need to determine if this FuncLit is the root? Body is not FuncLit.
				// Skip descending
				return false
			}
			if d, ok := n.(*ast.DeferStmt); ok {
				defers = append(defers, d)
			}
			return true
		})
		if len(defers) == 0 {
			return
		}
		// find exit calls anywhere (excluding nested func lit)
		firstDeferText := ctx.nodeText(defers[0].Call) // defer call expr? DeferStmt.Call is CallExpr; text like "os.Remove(fn)"
		// In message, they show `defer os.Remove(fn)` including defer keyword. So construct: "defer "+callText
		ast.Inspect(body, func(n ast.Node) bool {
			if _, ok := n.(*ast.FuncLit); ok {
				return false
			}
			call, ok := n.(*ast.CallExpr)
			if !ok {
				return true
			}
			fname := ctx.callFuncName(call)
			exitName := ""
			isExit := false
			switch fname {
			case "log.Fatal", "log.Fatalf", "log.Fatalln", "os.Exit":
				exitName = fname
				isExit = true
			default:
				// also log.Panic? probably not exit
				// selector .Fatal etc from log?
				if sel, ok := selectorOf(call.Fun); ok {
					if sel.Sel.Name == "Exit" {
						// os.Exit already covered
					}
				}
			}
			if isExit {
				// only if defer is before this call? Position order: defer pos < call pos
				if defers[0].Pos() < call.Pos() {
					out = append(out, ctx.warn(call.Pos(), "%s will exit, and `defer %s` will not run", exitName, firstDeferText))
				}
			}
			return true
		})
	}
	walkFile(lf, func(n ast.Node) bool {
		switch v := n.(type) {
		case *ast.FuncDecl:
			if v.Body != nil {
				processFuncBody(v.Body)
			}
		case *ast.FuncLit:
			if v.Body != nil {
				processFuncBody(v.Body)
			}
		}
		return true
	})
	return out
}

func (ctx *checkerContext) isImportedName(name string) bool {
	// check imports in all files of package
	for _, lf := range ctx.pkg.Files {
		if lf.AST == nil {
			continue
		}
		for _, imp := range lf.AST.Imports {
			path, _ := strconv.Unquote(imp.Path.Value)
			if imp.Name != nil {
				if imp.Name.Name == name {
					return true
				}
			} else {
				if pkgPathLast(path) == name {
					return true
				}
			}
		}
	}
	return false
}

package main

import (
	"fmt"

)

func init() {
	register("appendAssign", checkAppendAssign)
	register("appendCombine", checkAppendCombine)
	register("argOrder", checkArgOrder)
	register("assignOp", checkAssignOp)
	register("badCall", checkBadCall)
	register("badCond", checkBadCond)
	register("captLocal", checkCaptLocal)
	register("caseOrder", checkCaseOrder)
	register("codegenComment", checkCodegenComment)
	register("commentFormatting", checkCommentFormatting)

	register("dupBranchBody", checkDupBranchBody)
	register("dupCase", checkDupCase)
	register("dupSubExpr", checkDupSubExpr)
func checkCommentFormatting(ctx *checkerContext, lf *loadedFile) []warning {
	var out []warning
	if lf.AST == nil {
		return out
	}
	for _, cg := range lf.AST.Comments {
		for _, c := range cg.List {
			txt := c.Text
			if !strings.HasPrefix(txt, "//") {
				continue
			}
			if txt == "//" {
				continue
			}
			rest := txt[2:]
			if rest == "" {
				continue
			}
			// directives: //go:, //line, // +build, //go:build, etc (?) check first char
			if strings.HasPrefix(txt, "//go:") || strings.HasPrefix(txt, "//line") || strings.HasPrefix(txt, "// +build") || strings.HasPrefix(txt, "//go:build") {
				continue
			}
			// if rest starts with space or tab or / (///) or !? probe showed /// and //! not flagged, tab?
			// Original flagged //This and //bad, not /// / //! / //\t
			first := rest[0]
			if first == ' ' || first == '\t' || first == '/' || first == '!' {
				continue
			}
			out = append(out, ctx.warn(c.Pos(), "put a space between `//` and comment text"))
			break
		}
	}
	return out
}

func checkDupCase(ctx *checkerContext, lf *loadedFile) []warning {
	var out []warning
	walkFile(lf, func(n ast.Node) bool {
		var list []ast.Stmt
		switch v := n.(type) {
		case *ast.SwitchStmt:
			if v.Body != nil {
				list = v.Body.List
			}
		case *ast.TypeSwitchStmt:
			if v.Body != nil {
				list = v.Body.List
			}
		case *ast.SelectStmt:
			if v.Body != nil {
				list = v.Body.List
			}
		default:
			return true
		}
		// collect case exprs across all clauses in this switch
		seen := map[string]ast.Expr{}
		for _, stmt := range list {
			var exprs []ast.Expr
			var clause ast.Node
			switch cc := stmt.(type) {
			case *ast.CaseClause:
				exprs = cc.List
				clause = cc
			case *ast.CommClause:
				// comm clause comm is statement, not case expr - dupCase probably only switch
				_ = clause
				continue
			}
			for _, e := range exprs {
				key := ctx.formatNode(e)
				if _, dup := seen[key]; dup {
					out = append(out, ctx.warn(e.Pos(), "'case %s' is duplicated", ctx.nodeText(e)))
				} else {
					seen[key] = e
				}
				_ = clause
			}
		}
		return true
	})
	return out
}

func checkIndexAlloc(ctx *checkerContext, lf *loadedFile) []warning {
	var out []warning
	walkFile(lf, func(n ast.Node) bool {
		call, ok := n.(*ast.CallExpr)
		if !ok || len(call.Args) != 2 {
			return true
		}
		fname := ctx.callFuncName(call)
		if fname != "strings.Index" && fname != "strings.IndexByte" && fname != "strings.IndexRune" {
			// Probe: strings.Index(string(x), y)
			if fname != "strings.Index" {
				return true
			}
		}
		// first arg is string(x) conversion where x is []byte
		conv, ok := unparen(call.Args[0]).(*ast.CallExpr)
		if !ok || len(conv.Args) != 1 {
			return true
		}
		// conv.Fun is type string
		if !isIdent(conv.Fun, "string") {
			// type conversion fun may be Ident string or type expr - nodeText
			if ctx.nodeText(conv.Fun) != "string" {
				return true
			}
		}
		x := conv.Args[0]
		sugCall := fmt.Sprintf("bytes.Index(%s, []byte(%s))", ctx.nodeText(x), ctx.nodeText(call.Args[1]))
		// But if IndexByte etc suggestion differs; for Index probe exact
		out = append(out, ctx.warn(call.Pos(), "consider replacing %s with %s", ctx.nodeText(call), sugCall))
		return true
	})
	return out
}

func (b *Builder) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
	b.copyCheck()

// WriteByte appends the byte c to b's buffer.

func (b *Builder) WriteByte(c byte) error {

// are the same length and contain the same bytes.

	// Neither cmd/compile nor gccgo allocates for these string conversions.
	return string(a) == string(b)

// Compare returns an integer comparing two byte slices lexicographically.
// The result will be 0 if a == b, -1 if a < b, and +1 if a > b.
// A nil argument is equivalent to an empty slice.

func benchmarkCompareBytesBigUnaligned(b *testing.B, offset int) {
	b.StopTimer()
	b1 := make([]byte, 0, 1<<20)
	for len(b1) < 1<<20 {
		b1 = append(b1, "Hello Gophers!"...)
	}
	b2 := append([]byte("12345678")[:offset], b1...)
	b.StartTimer()
	for j := 0; j < b.N; j++ {

// pin pins the current goroutine to P, disables preemption and
// returns poolLocal pool for the P and the P's id.
// Caller must call runtime_procUnpin() when done with the pool.
func (p *Pool) pin() (*poolLocal, int) {
	pid := runtime_procPin()
	// In pinSlow we store to local and then to localSize, here we load in opposite order.
	// Since we've disabled preemption, GC cannot happen in between.
	// Thus here we must observe local at least as large localSize.
	// We can observe a newer/larger local, it is fine (we must observe its zero-initialized-ness).
	s := runtime_LoadAcquintptr(&p.localSize) // load-acquire
	l := p.local                              // load-consume
	if uintptr(pid) < s {
		return indexLocal(l, pid), pid
	}
	return p.pinSlow()
}

func checkParamTypeCombine(ctx *checkerContext, lf *loadedFile) []warning {
	var out []warning
	checkFuncType := func(ft *ast.FuncType, pos token.Pos, recv *ast.FieldList) {
		if ft == nil {
			return
		}
		// Need to detect adjacent fields with same type but separate names, or repeated single-name fields
		// Original triggers for: func(a int, b int, ...) / func(format string) (index int, wid int, ok bool) where results also combinable
		// It reports once per function with full suggested signature (including params and results combined).
		// Determine if any combining possible in Params or Results.
		canCombineParams := fieldListCanCombine(ctx, ft.Params)
		canCombineResults := fieldListCanCombine(ctx, ft.Results)
		if !canCombineParams && !canCombineResults {
			return
		}
		orig := buildFuncSignature(ctx, ft, recv, false)
		sug := buildFuncSignature(ctx, ft, recv, true)
		if orig == sug {
			return
		}
		out = append(out, ctx.warn(pos, "%s could be replaced with %s", orig, sug))
	}
	walkFile(lf, func(n ast.Node) bool {
		switch v := n.(type) {
		case *ast.FuncDecl:
			checkFuncType(v.Type, v.Pos(), v.Recv)
			// return false to avoid duplicate FuncType visit below? But Walk will still visit Type node as FuncType case and duplicate.
			// Our switch includes FuncType case; to avoid, we should not handle FuncType separately for FuncDecls.
			// Since Inspect visits children regardless, FuncType node will be visited next and check again with same pos (FuncType.Pos, not FuncDecl.Pos)
			// Problem: original position for FuncDecl is decl pos (1:1) not type pos. If FuncType check also runs, position would be slightly differ and duplicate.
			// So we will handle FuncType only if it's not part of FuncDecl/FuncLit? Hard.
			// Solution: Do NOT register FuncType handling in walk; only FuncDecl and FuncLit and maybe type declarations `type F func(...)`
		case *ast.FuncLit:
			checkFuncType(v.Type, v.Pos(), nil)
		}
		return true
	})
	return out
}

func checkImportShadow(ctx *checkerContext, lf *loadedFile) []warning {
	var out []warning
	// Local definitions shadowing import names (package scope imports of this file)
	type impEntry struct {
		path     string
		hasAlias bool
	}
	importNames := map[string]impEntry{}
	if lf.AST != nil {
		for _, imp := range lf.AST.Imports {
			name := ""
			hasAlias := false
			pth, _ := strconv.Unquote(imp.Path.Value)
			if imp.Name != nil {
				name = imp.Name.Name
				hasAlias = true
			} else {
				name = pkgPathLast(pth)
			}
			if name != "" && name != "_" && name != "." {
				importNames[name] = impEntry{path: pth, hasAlias: hasAlias}
			}
		}
	}
	if len(importNames) == 0 {
		return out
	}
	report := func(id *ast.Ident) {
		if id != nil {
			if ent, ok := importNames[id.Name]; ok {
				if ent.hasAlias {
					out = append(out, ctx.warn(id.Pos(), "shadow of imported from '%s' package '%s'", ent.path, id.Name))
				} else {
					out = append(out, ctx.warn(id.Pos(), "shadow of imported package '%s'", id.Name))
				}
			}
		}
	}
	walkFile(lf, func(n ast.Node) bool {
		switch v := n.(type) {
		case *ast.AssignStmt:
			if v.Tok == token.DEFINE {
				for _, lhs := range v.Lhs {
					if id, ok := lhs.(*ast.Ident); ok {
						report(id)
					}
				}
			}
		case *ast.RangeStmt:
			// range variables are not flagged by builtinShadow (observed)
			_ = v
		case *ast.FuncDecl:
			// params / receiver / results names?
			// Check fields
			if v.Type != nil {
				if v.Type.Params != nil {
					for _, f := range v.Type.Params.List {
						for _, nm := range f.Names {
							report(nm)
						}
					}
				}
				if v.Type.Results != nil {
					for _, f := range v.Type.Results.List {
						for _, nm := range f.Names {
							report(nm)
						}
					}
				}
			}
			if v.Recv != nil {
				for _, f := range v.Recv.List {
					for _, nm := range f.Names {
						report(nm)
					}
				}
			}
		case *ast.FuncLit:
			if v.Type != nil {
				if v.Type.Params != nil {
					for _, f := range v.Type.Params.List {
						for _, nm := range f.Names {
							report(nm)
						}
					}
				}
				if v.Type.Results != nil {
					for _, f := range v.Type.Results.List {
						for _, nm := range f.Names {
							report(nm)
						}
					}
				}
			}
		case *ast.ValueSpec:
			// local? global vars also shadow import in file scope? importShadow may flag var decls
			for _, nm := range v.Names {
				report(nm)
			}
		}
		return true
	})
	return out
}

func checkAppendAssign(ctx *checkerContext, lf *loadedFile) []warning {
	var out []warning
	walkFile(lf, func(n ast.Node) bool {
		as, ok := n.(*ast.AssignStmt)
		if !ok || len(as.Lhs) != 1 || len(as.Rhs) != 1 {
			return true
		}
		call, ok := unparen(as.Rhs[0]).(*ast.CallExpr)
		if !ok {
			return true
		}
		id, ok := unparen(call.Fun).(*ast.Ident)
		if !ok || id.Name != "append" || len(call.Args) < 1 {
			return true
		}
		first := unparen(call.Args[0])
		// Only consider tracked slice forms
		tracked := false
		switch first.(type) {
		case *ast.Ident, *ast.SelectorExpr, *ast.IndexExpr, *ast.IndexListExpr, *ast.SliceExpr, *ast.StarExpr:
			tracked = true
		}
		if !tracked {
			return true
		}
		// If first arg is a slice/index of an array, skip (no slice variable to assign back to)
		if _, isSlice := first.(*ast.SliceExpr); isSlice {
			base := first
			for {
				switch b := base.(type) {
				case *ast.SliceExpr:
					base = b.X
				case *ast.IndexExpr:
					base = b.X
				case *ast.ParenExpr:
					base = b.X
				case *ast.StarExpr:
					base = b.X
				default:
					goto doneBase
				}
			}
		doneBase:
			if bt := ctx.exprType(base); bt != nil {
				if _, isArr := bt.Underlying().(*types.Array); isArr {
					return true
				}
			}
		}
		if !ctx.exprEq(as.Lhs[0], call.Args[0]) {
			out = append(out, ctx.warn(call.Pos(), "append result not assigned to the same slice"))
		}
		return true
	})
	return out
}

package main

type ruleguardState struct {
	rules      []rgParsedRule
	rawFiles   []string
	loadErrors []string
}

type rgParsedRule struct {
	group string
	// parsed patterns from a very small subset of gorule DSL
	patterns []rgPattern
}

type rgPattern struct {
	matchText  string // original pattern source e.g. `$x`
	importPath string
	funcName   string // e.g. fmt.Sprintf etc if any
	msg        string
	suggest    string
	whereExpr  string
	file       string
}

func prepareRuleguard(enabled []string) *ruleguardState {
	st := &ruleguardState{}
	for _, e := range enabled {
		if e == "ruleguard" {
			st.loadRuleguardRules()
			break
		}
	}
	return st
}

func (st *ruleguardState) loadRuleguardRules() {
	if paramRuleguardRules == "" {
		return
	}
	// Validate failOn
	failOnSet := map[string]bool{}
	if paramRuleguardFailOn != "" {
		for _, tok := range strings.Split(paramRuleguardFailOn, ",") {
			if tok != "dsl" && tok != "import" && tok != "all" {
				msg := fmt.Sprintf("'failOnError' flag '%s' is invalid. It must be a comma-separated list and supported values are 'dsl,import,all'", paramRuleguardFailOn)
				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\tdebug: ruleguard: initialization failure: ruleguard init error: %s\n", msg)
				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "init checkers: ruleguard init error: %s\n", msg)
				os.Exit(1)
			}
			failOnSet[tok] = true
		}
	}
	fatal := paramRuleguardFailOnError || failOnSet["all"] || failOnSet["dsl"]
	patterns := strings.Split(paramRuleguardRules, ",")
	for _, pat := range patterns {
		matches, _ := filepath.Glob(pat)
		if len(matches) == 0 {
			msg := fmt.Sprintf("no file matching '%s'", pat)
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\tdebug: ruleguard: initialization failure: ruleguard init error: %s\n", msg)
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "init checkers: ruleguard init error: %s\n", msg)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		st.rawFiles = append(st.rawFiles, matches...)
		for _, f := range matches {
			loadErr := st.tryLoadRuleFile(f)
			if loadErr != "" {
				if fatal {
					fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\tdebug: ruleguard: initialization failure: ruleguard init error: %s\n", loadErr)
					fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "init checkers: ruleguard init error: %s\n", loadErr)
					os.Exit(1)
				}
				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "ruleguard init error, skip %s: %s\n", f, loadErr)
				continue
			}
		}
	}
	if len(st.rules) == 0 {
		st.emptyAfterLoad = true
	}
}

func runRuleguardRules(ctx *checkerContext, lf *loadedFile) []warning {
	// If no custom rules, embedded rules currently unknown - return none
	if ctx.rg == nil || len(ctx.rg.rules) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	// Very simple matcher: if match pattern is a literal call pattern like `fmt.Sprint($x)` we attempt textual matching using source.
	// For each AST call node, compare its normalized text template where $var wildcards match any expr.
	var out []warning
	for _, rule := range ctx.rg.rules {
		for _, pat := range rule.patterns {
			// skip complex patterns with Where etc.
			patText := strings.TrimSpace(pat.matchText)
			// Patterns may contain $$ etc.
			walkFile(lf, func(n ast.Node) bool {
				if call, ok := n.(*ast.CallExpr); ok {
					// textual template match roughly: replace $identifier in patText with wildcard; check if call text matches skeleton (func name part)
					if ruleguardMatchCall(ctx, patText, call) {
						msg := pat.msg

						msg = substituteRuleVars(msg, patText, ctx, call)
						out = append(out, ctx.warn(call.Pos(), "%s", msg))
					}
				}
				return true
			})
		}
	}
	return out
}
